title: How does the TikTok algorithm work? Your For You feed
caption:
TikTok bet you'd watch this. So how does the TikTok algorithm decide what to show you?
Every finish, skip, replay and second you linger is a clue. And a stranger who watched the same two videos as you may help pick your next one.
Did you finish this one? Yes or no?

youtube_title: The Stranger Who Picks Your TikTok Feed 😮
youtube_description:
How does the TikTok algorithm decide what to show you? If you're watching this on TikTok's For You feed, TikTok bet you'd watch it before you saw it. (On YouTube, YouTube's own system made that call.)

TikTok says it gives each candidate video a prediction score, an estimate of how likely you are to interact with it, and serves the highest scores to your For You feed. The clues include videos you watched, finished, liked or skipped, your replays, and how long you spend on a video. TikTok calls finishing a longer video from beginning to end a strong indicator of interest.

The twist is TikTok's own example: if another user engaged with two of the same videos as you, the system may predict you'll engage with a third video that person engaged with. So a stranger you'll never meet can help pick your feed.

In 2021 the New York Times saw an internal TikTok document called "TikTok Algo 101", which TikTok confirmed was authentic. It said TikTok optimizes for two closely related metrics: retention (whether you come back) and time spent.

Fine print: "bet" is our word for TikTok's prediction score. TikTok doesn't publish how its model is built; the two phones are an illustration of its own example. The "TikTok Algo 101" page in the video is re-created: only its title and the two metric names come from the New York Times report. No real TikTok interface or logo is shown; the phone and the videos in it are drawn by hand.

Sources:
- TikTok Transparency Center, "Introduction to the TikTok recommendation system" (read Oct 24, 2026): https://www.tiktok.com/transparency/en-us/recommendation-system/
- TikTok Newsroom, "How TikTok recommends videos #ForYou" (June 18, 2020): https://newsroom.tiktok.com/en-us/how-tiktok-recommends-videos-for-you
